summary: Tested the All-30-games enablement end to end on the public URL. Working: GC Settings L9, L10 and Champion selects each offer 31 options (Colour Match plus 30 games), with L1-8 locked. Saving and applying sudoku_mini/maze_solver/lights_out produced the notice 'Applied to Levels 9, 10 + Champion game' and the schedule cards updated. GC4 was then restored (L9 colour_match 5/10 with 50/40/30/20/10, L10 number_sequence with 9/8/7/6/5, Champion colour_match 6/20) and checked via the API. Preview game select lists 31 options and the Memory Match board works. The Paid World contest-game-select shows 30 games in 6 groups (4/3/6/6/7/4). Editing an existing contest saves game_type for Vol.2 games. All 30 games render with no JS errors and no horizontal overflow at 1920px and 390px (admin Test-game modal). number_sequence, tower_of_hanoi and maze_solver were played to completion on both viewports. PlayGame on mobile with a maze_solver contest ticket: captcha verify, submit, score 100 and attempts 2 to 1. API: /api/games/submit for a nonogram_mini ticket decrements attempts, the 3rd attempt returns 400, and the leaderboard shows the entry. Impossible Challenges is unchanged (only the Add Number Sequence and Add Colour Match buttons). Free World Pause/Resume works and was left RESUMED. Main problem found: POST /api/admin/contests ignores game_type and the other skill-engine fields, so a contest created in the Create dialog is saved with game_type=None.

critical.issue: create_contest_api builds Contest(...) from a fixed field list and never saves payload.game_type (also entry_mode, attempts_per_ticket, max_attempts, winner_selection_method, engine_type and the other extended fields). The Create Contest dialog sends game_type='maze_solver' etc., the toast says 'Contest created', but the DB has game_type=None. /api/games/submit then returns 400 'This contest is not tied to a game'. Reproduced: POST with game_type nonogram_mini gave db game_type None. PUT /api/admin/contests/{id} does save it correctly. Fix: after Contest(...).model_dump(), copy the same allowed keys used by update_contest_full (or call that update logic) into doc before insert_one.

minor.issue: For the 28 client games the server trusts body.solved=true from the browser; only duration is server-measured. A scripted client can claim 'solved' straight away with a time-based score for Every-Level Bonus Tokens or Champion prizes. Accepted by design for now; consider requiring a server-checkable answer for reward-bearing levels.

ui_bugs.issue: Accuracy uses a hardcoded optimal=(n-2)*2=10 steps, but the randomized DFS maze often has a longer shortest path (BFS found 16 steps, giving 63% accuracy for a perfect run). Accuracy is 60% of Paid World points, so players are unfairly penalised depending on the random maze, which matters now that maze_solver can be picked for paid contests. Compute optimal with BFS on the generated maze.

Switching a level from colour_match to another game keeps the stale game_config {colours, rounds} in the saved draft. Harmless today because the backend ignores it for client games, but it is untidy. Reset game_config when game_id changes.
The Memory board stays on screen after the preview game is switched to another game (e.g. nonogram_mini). Only Memory Match can be played in Preview; other games just set the config.

rca of the issue: Create-contest game_type loss: backend/routers/admin_routes.py create_contest_api (lines ~1421-1459) builds the doc only from Contest(...) with explicit fields plus skill_question_type/difficulty, and never reads payload['game_type']. Repro: POST /api/admin/contests {title, prize_amount:10, game_type:'nonogram_mini'} gives db.contests.game_type None. Mitigation: merge the allowed payload keys (same set as update_contest_full) into doc before insert, and validate game_type against GAME_TYPES.
